transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Dubois. I am Dr. Miller. Please, have a seat.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I asked to see you because there has been a mistake regarding your diagnostic results. To be precise, there was a mix-up in our scheduling system between you and another patient with a very similar name. Because of this, you were given the wrong lab reports and told you had a chronic kidney condition that you do not actually have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am sorry? What are you saying?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means that the diagnosis you were given last week is incorrect. You are not sick with that condition. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand. Last Tuesday, I was told my kidneys were failing. I have spent four days thinking my life was changing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, as I said, the files were swapped. You received another man's results. Just to be sure we are on the same page, do you understand that the previous diagnosis was a mistake caused by a name mix-up?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. I understand the words. But I do not understand how this happens. I felt... I felt a great shame. I told my daughter I was ill. I felt so small.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system has a glitch when names are similar. It happens occasionally in a large hospital.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Occasionnally? C'est absurde! My dignity, my peace of mind, you throw it away because of a name?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The important thing is that your labs are actually normal.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You do not seem to see the problem. I have been terrified. I have been preparing for a death that is not coming.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, looking at the actual chart, your creatinine levels are perfectly fine, which means your kidney function is normal.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not care about the levels! I care that you lied to me for a week!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, the error occurred because the records were misfiled in the electronic portal.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like a fool. A complete idiot. Je me sens humilié.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's just move forward. I need to make sure we fix this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are just speaking of files. I am speaking of my heart.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, but the facts are that you are healthy. If we dwell on the emotion, we can't get to the solution.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: There is no apology. Not one word.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The administrative process for these errors is quite complex, but we are auditing the file now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not even looking at me. You are looking at your tablet.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm just checking the timeline. Look, I really have to get to another clinic in ten minutes, so let's wrap this up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are rushing me? After you told me I was dying?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am simply trying to be efficient with the plan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot believe this. The arrogance.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Here is what we will do. I am going to print out your actual, correct lab results right now. I will hand them to you in a folder. You should take these home and show them to your daughter so she knows you are healthy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will enter a correction note in your permanent medical record by the end of the day today. That way, any other doctor who sees your file will know the previous diagnosis was a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And how do I know this will not happen again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system is being updated. Now, do you have your folder?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have it. But I feel nothing but anger.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But as I said, I have to go. You have the correct papers now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not how a doctor speaks to a man.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medical facts are corrected, Mr. Dubois. That is the priority. Good day.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('wrap this up', 'have to get to another clinic', 'have to go') and shows defensive escalation.

E.justification: Error named in first turn, lay language used, and comprehension checked twice ('Does that make sense so far?', 'do you understand...?').

A.justification: No direct apology language used and responsibility is deflected to the 'scheduling system' and 'electronic portal'.

R.justification: Patient's emotional bids are consistently met with factual redirection ('The important thing is...', 'the facts are...').

T.justification: Specific steps provided with timelines (print now, correction note by end of day), patient role (take folder home to daughter), and prevention (system being updated).
